Expectation1: Maintain regular communication with family members
Situation1: A family member has a new job and has shared some initial excitement about it with their relatives.
Expectation2: Ensure compliance with safety and regulatory standards
Situation2: An external inspector has raised immediate concerns that could halt operations unless issues are resolved
Story: I sat at my desk, the hum of the office barely registering as I stared at the blinking cursor on my screen. My phone buzzed with a message from my daughter: “Dad, can you call tonight? Jamie wants to tell you all about her new job!” I smiled, picturing my granddaughter’s eager face, remembering how important it is to be present, to listen, to celebrate these milestones with her. But just as I reached for my phone, my email chimed—urgent, flagged red. The external inspector’s report was attached, outlining safety concerns that, if not addressed immediately, could shut down our entire operation. My team was waiting for my guidance, expecting me to lead, to ensure every standard was met without delay. I felt the weight of both worlds pressing in—my family needing my attention, my team needing my expertise. My heart tugged toward home, but my mind raced with calculations and compliance checklists. I sat there, torn, the demands of grandparent and engineer pulling me in opposite directions, unsure which call to answer first.
